title: Access Proofflow & Role Delegation Guidelines
body:
Purpose:
This note defines a repeatable "proofflow" for role delegation and evidence handoff across Redwood's three hosting tiers (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to make RBAC v2 delegation decisions auditable, machine-checkable, and exportable to SIEMs with minimal transformation.

Scope:
- Applies to administrative and elevated-role delegations (role activation, emergency access, service account impersonation).
- Covers artifact types required for compliance requests and automated evidence pipelines.
- Prescribes SIEM export fields and mapping to our audit schema.

High-level principles (short):
- Minimal, reversible delegation: grant just-enough, time-bound, and with an activation ticket/justification token.
- Canonical evidence bundle: every delegation must produce a standard set of artifacts (request, approval, activation, deactivation).
- Deterministic enrichment: metadata fields used by downstream automation must be present and stable across environments.

Canonical evidence bundle (required artifacts):
1) Delegation Request: user, requested-role, scope (tenant/org), reason, request-id, timestamp.
2) Approval Record: approver(s), approval-type (auto/manual/policy), auth-ticket-id, TTL, timestamp.
3) Activation Event: who activated, method (console/CLI/api), session-id, target-credentials (masked), activation-timestamp.
4) Usage Snapshot: sample of privileged API calls (first N calls or summary), token/kvs key-churn events.
5) Deactivation Record: who/what ended access, deactivation-timestamp, leakage-check-run-id.
6) Evidence digest: SHA256 of all artifacts (stored in evidence-store), evidence-store-path.

Environment-by-environment rules (short):
- Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood-hosted):
  * Delegation must be brokered by Redwood control-plane. No direct tenant-managed role creation for infra-level roles.
  * Approvals: at least 2 approvers for infra/elevated roles; can be policy-driven for low-risk app roles.
  * SIEM exports: mask tenant identifiers with pseudonym_id unless customer consented for full-tenancy telemetry.
  * Evidence TTL: keep full evidence for 365 days, low-res summary for 3 years.

- Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity):
  * Delegations may be initiated by customer admins; Redwood must receive an approval ticket for platform-level escalations.
  * Approvals: customer config determines approver set. Platform-level role delegation requires Redwood SRE approval for changes to serving runtime.
  * SIEM exports: send full tenant_id when contract allows, else pseudonymize. Add "dedicated_pool" context field.
  * Evidence TTL: configurable per customer contract, default 1 year.

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  * Delegation model is customer-controlled. Redwood only receives evidence artifacts when customer-configured audit forwarding is enabled.
  * For air-gapped/private installs, include an "evidence-manifest" file that operators can export on-demand.
  * SIEM exports: optional. If enabled, must map local account ids to canonical customer guid.

RBAC v2 delegation patterns (recommended templates):
1) Scoped-Proxy Delegation: create a short-lived proxy token with (role, tenant-scope) and require an activation ticket. Good for automated jobs.
2) Elevation-with-Justification: user requests elevation; an approver signs the auth-ticket; activation requires CLI/console with ticket.
3) Service-To-Service Impersonation: services call identity-service to mint ephemeral creds; every mint includes callsite, calling-service, and reason.

Minimum audit-log schema additions (fields we require for delegation traces):
- event.type (delegation.request|delegation.approval|delegation.activation|delegation.deactivation|evidence.export)
- event.id (uuid)
- actor.id (principal id)
- actor.type (user|service|system)
- target.role (role name)
- target.scope (tenant|org|resource-path)
- request.id (request-id)
- auth.ticket (opaque id)
- approvers (array of principal ids)  -- NOTE: in logs we carry a comma-separated list string for SIEMs that don't support arrays
- method (cli|console|api|operator)
- session.id
- evidence.digest
- evidence.store.path
- mask.level (none|pseudonym|redacted)
- env (hosted|dedicated|private)
- timestamp

Example log line (JSON payload as string to be sent to event pipeline):
{
  "event.type": "delegation.activation",
  "event.id": "e3f2a7b8-9c4e-4a1d-bf6a-8c3b2d5e7f9a",
  "actor.id": "u-1543",
  "actor.type": "user",
  "target.role": "infra-admin",
  "target.scope": "tenant:acme-corp",
  "request.id": "req-2024-11-05-21",
  "auth.ticket": "auth-87a1",
  "approvers": "u-77,u-98",
  "method": "cli",
  "session.id": "sess-9b2",
  "evidence.digest": "sha256:abcd...",
  "evidence.store.path": "s3://evidence/hosted/2024/11/req-2024-11-05-21/",
  "mask.level": "pseudonym",
  "env": "hosted",
  "timestamp": "2024-11-05T21:12:03Z"
}

Note on arrays: our export format uses strings for small arrays (comma-separated) because several SIEM endpoints cannot accept nested arrays. Explainers in the evidence pipeline will rehydrate arrays for ingest consumers.

SIEM field mapping recommendations (common destination names):
- sourcetype -> redwood:rbac_delegation
- host -> redwood-region
- _time -> timestamp
- user -> actor.id
- action -> event.type
- extra -> json payload (the full payload as above)

Policy template (AWS-style snippet for delegation activation role) - example to be adapted per provider:
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "ScopedDelegationActivation",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["sts:AssumeRole"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-delegation-hosted-InfraAdmin"],
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {
          "redwood:AuthTicketId": "${aws:RequestTag/auth-ticket-id}"
        },
        "Bool": {"aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent": "true"}
      }
    }
  ]
}

Operational playbook (short steps for an RBAC delegation lifecycle):
1) Request: user opens request portal (request-id generated). Tag request with risk-level and resource-scope.
2) Policy check: system performs automated policy gating for low-risk requests.
3) Approval: approver(s) provide approval recorded into ticketing system; an auth-ticket is minted.
4) Activation: user presents auth-ticket via cli/console to perform activation; activation event is emitted and evidence bundle started.
5) Monitor: system records the first N privileged operations and a daily summary while active.
6) Deactivate: either TTL expiry or explicit deactivation; deactivation event emitted and evidence bundle sealed.
7) Export: evidence digest and manifest are forwarded to SIEM/evidence-store URL according to environment policies.

Automation considerations and implementation notes:
- Evidence-store design: prefer write-once object storage with an index service that stores evidence digests + metadata. Evidence objects should be immutable and signed.
- Signature chain: each artifact gets a signing key; consider HSM/KMS for hosted-dedicated keys.
- SIEM batching: implement a transform layer that converts our canonical payloads to target vendor payloads (Splunk/Datadog/Exabeam). Keep an adapter table.
- Pseudonymization: central service issues stable pseudonym ids for tenant principals to maintain cross-tenant analytics while preserving customer privacy.

Checklist for onboarding a new delegation flow (quick):
- [ ] Define role and scope clearly (resource paths).
- [ ] Decide default mask.level for environment.
- [ ] Configure approver set and escalation cadence.
- [ ] Hook evidence-store path and retention policy.
- [ ] Map out SIEM export fields and adapter.
- [ ] Add automated tests that assert evidence bundle completeness.

Open questions / decisions to escalate:
- How long should pseudonymized identifiers be retained vs fully redacted when customers request data deletion?
- SLA for retrieval of sealed evidence bundles in private/on-prem installs (proposal: 72 hours).
- Standardized TTLs per risk class (proposal: low=30d, medium=180d, high=365d).

Appendix: brief glossary
- auth-ticket: short-lived token representing an approval record.
- evidence digest: cryptographic hash summarizing all artifacts for a delegation instance.
- pseudonym_id: reversible token used in hosted analytics to represent tenant identities without shipping PII to third-party SIEMs.

End of doc. For implementation tasks, see linked artifacts and jira:SEC-8721 for the automation backlog.
